sections.h2: Ways to sell a house fast in Hillsborough
sections.html:
You can go three ways in Hillsborough: list with an agent, sell on your own, or find a cash buyer willing to take the house as is. The township lies in Somerset County, in the Raritan Valley.

What sets the pace is paperwork more than price. The smoke detector certificate, open building permits and your tax record determine how soon a closing can be scheduled.

  • Agent listing: most exposure, though showings, the buyer's mortgage and a repair list each add weeks.
  • Without an agent: the commission stays in your pocket, while pricing, the contract and the alarm inspection become your job.
  • Cash buyer: no lender and no repair talks, which leaves title work and the certificate inspection as the main clock.

Judge each route by what you keep after fees and repairs.

Hillsborough Township is large, at 55.10 square miles, and includes communities such as Belle Mead, Neshanic, Flagtown, Amwell and Woods Tavern. Nearly 40 percent of the land is protected or preserved open space, including Duke Farms, a 2,700 acre estate in the northeast corner. A house near preserved land often keeps its farm or woodland views for good.

About 79.5 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, and an owned home has a median value of $547,600. Owners carrying a mortgage spend a median of $3,017 a month on housing, and owners without one spend $1,470. The township has 16,388 households with a median income of $154,031, and turnover is low, since 91.1 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. Population is estimated at 45,061, up 4.1 percent from 2020.

Expect a commuter household with solid income as your buyer, and expect to compete with only a modest supply of similar homes. Buyers who need cash certainty or no financing contingency are a smaller group, but a real one.

sections.h2: Commute and schools buyers ask about
sections.html:
Ask any Hillsborough agent and you will hear that commute and school questions come before kitchen questions.

  • Roads: U.S. Route 206 is the main route. A 3.75 mile bypass finished in 2021, and the old road is meant to become a downtown main street. County Routes 514 and 533 also cross the township, while Interstate 287 sits just outside in Bridgewater and Franklin.
  • Transit: D.H.I.L.A.N. buses link to Manville, Bridgewater and Somerville, and Coach USA runs four weekday morning express trips to Midtown Manhattan.
  • Schools: the Hillsborough Township School District runs pre-kindergarten through grade 12 in nine schools, including five K to 4 elementaries, Auten Road Intermediate for grades 5 and 6, a middle school for 7 and 8 and the high school.

Four offices have a hand in a Hillsborough closing: the Fire Safety Department, the Building Department, the Tax Collector and the Somerset County Clerk.

Hillsborough seller checklist
TaskOfficeWhat to know
Smoke detector certificationFire Safety DepartmentFor a resale, the Building Department does not issue a certificate of occupancy. Schedule this inspection instead.
Open permitsBuilding DepartmentThe current owner must close any open permit, even one pulled by a previous owner.
Quarterly taxesTax CollectorBilled on the first of February, May, August and November. Payment is on time through the 10th.
Deed recordingSomerset County ClerkA county cover sheet goes with every deed. The first page costs $45 and each added page $10.

The township's SDL portal shows permit status and inspection results, so pull the permit history for your address early. Fixing a stale permit takes less time than explaining it to a buyer's attorney.

An estimated third-quarter bill goes out each July, figured from the current year's assessed value. Multiplying it by four gives a wrong annual number, because adjustments land in the third and fourth quarters.

The township runs a reassessment each year, so assessed values track the market. The rate fell from $2.419 per $100 of assessed value in 2018 to $2.143 in 2024, even as values climbed. A check mailed on the 9th but received on the 12th is late, because the office ignores postmarks.

If you pay by ACH direct debit, tell the Tax Collector as soon as you list, since debits continue until the office is notified. A seller with unpaid taxes should request a payoff figure ahead of closing. Delinquent charges can end up in the township's online tax lien auction, so clear them before a buyer's title search turns them up.

Appeals go to the Somerset County Board of Taxation. The statewide date is April 1, pushed to May 1 in a district that has been revalued or reassessed, so ask the board or the township assessor which one fits your parcel. If the board rules against you, the Tax Court takes a petition for 45 days after the ruling.

sections.h2: State costs of selling in Hillsborough
sections.html:
When the deed is recorded, the state charges a Realty Transfer Fee, and it lands on the seller. A house priced near the Hillsborough median of $547,600 falls under the schedule for sales above $350,000, where the $4.80 per $500 band covers most of the price. Every band is posted by the Division of Taxation.

Sellers who remain New Jersey residents sign GIT/REP-3 at closing, which means no income tax is held back from the proceeds. If the house was your main home for two of the last five years, the federal gain exclusion that New Jersey follows may apply: $250,000 for one filer, $500,000 for joint filers.

A cash buyer skips the appraisal, the underwriting and the repair demands that tend to follow an inspection. Three things still apply: the township's smoke detector inspection, payoff of any taxes owed, and a recorded deed. Book the inspection once a contract is signed, look for open permits in the SDL portal, and get a payoff figure from the Tax Collector.

At the attorney's office, have your deed, a recent tax bill, any mortgage payoff letter and a list of open permits. A house in poor shape can still sell for cash, but any permit left open has to be closed by you, so settle that first and the closing date will hold.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Hillsborough house?
faqs.a: Not from the Building Department, which issues none for a residential resale. The Fire Safety Department handles a smoke detector certification inspection, and that is the visit you book. Your closing attorney can say whether a buyer's lender wants anything more.

faqs.q: When are Hillsborough property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are dated the first of February, May, August and November. Payment is on time through the 10th, or the next business day if the 10th is a weekend or holiday. Later payments owe interest back to the first, and postmarks do not count.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Hillsborough assessment?
faqs.a: Usually April 1, on Form A-1 with the Somerset County Board of Taxation. Where a revaluation or reassessment has been carried out the date shifts to May 1. The board or the township assessor can tell you which one governs your parcel.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when I sell in Hillsborough?
faqs.a: The Somerset County Clerk, whose office files deeds, mortgages and related papers. Every filing needs a county cover sheet, and recording costs $45 for page one and $10 for each page after. Your title company normally submits it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hillsborough house that has open permits or needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, though open permits stay attached to the house. Whoever owns the property must close an open permit, even one a prior owner pulled. Cash buyers will take a house needing repairs, but resolving the permit first avoids a snag at closing.
